title: Receipts/SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.cs: requirement test fails on base (2/3), passes on head (3/3); refutes 1 lens claim(s): requirement-tests-1

refutes.claim: No changed line mentions SuppressSourceGeneration. The TypeCollector edits only stop a crash on duplicate keys or mixed int/string keys: they `continue` after reporting DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys and skip `Dictionary.Add` on a repeated key. If 3.1.1 stopped analysing suppressed types for any other reason (an early exit or skip path for suppressed types), this change does not restore it. In that case a plain missing-[Key] violation on a `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]` type would still report no MsgPack004, and the main acceptance criterion is unmet. Meanwhile the README hunk documents that the analyzer validates these types.

title: Receipts/DuplicateKeySilentDropTests.cs: edge-case test passes on head (1 tests): no defect shown; refutes 2 lens claim(s): logic-edge-1, logic-edge-2

refutes.claim: The new `ContainsKey` guards swallow duplicate keys. Take a [MessagePackObject] with two distinct members, `[Key(0)] int FirstValue` and `[Key(0)] int SecondValue`. The first member is kept and the second is silently dropped from the generated formatter, so SecondValue is never serialized or deserialized. No diagnostic is reported. Before this change, `Dictionary.Add` threw, which surfaced as AD0001/CS8785 and so made the problem visible. The dynamic resolver rejects duplicate keys at runtime. The generated formatter now quietly loses data instead. The same applies to duplicate string keys (map mode) and to a property and a field sharing a key.

The same silent first-wins dedup is applied in the second member-collection block (fields/other path). For duplicate string keys it lets one member's data vanish from the generated map formatter, again with no diagnostic.
